text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: It costs y to take the test x.
Provide(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
Apply(x, y) ::: x can apply for financial aid from y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
Unemployed(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for y.
Premises:
Cost(gre, 205) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (Provide(ets, x) ↔ EconomicHardship(x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (EconomicHardship(x) ↔ (¬(Money(x) ∨ Resources(x)))) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
SingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
Unemployed(tomDad, moreThanAYear) ::: His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
Apply(tom, ets) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
